title: MZ Looking for some help modifying TP gain in relation to quantity of targets

posts.author: Niniann
Robro33
posts.body:
Niniann said:
Any help with this would be greatly appreciated, I've scoured google for a few hours at this point but haven't been able to find any concrete leads on how exactly to make the change I'm looking for.
Click to expand...
try removing the this.applyItemUserEffect(target) line from Game_Action.prototype.apply() entirely as apply() is ran per target, and then replicate it within something earlier on that gets ran per skill like BattleManager.startAction
Alternatively, flipping a switch or making a property somewhere within startAction(), using it to determine if applyItemUserEffect() gives the user TP at all, and then flipping the switch / deleting the property would also cause the effects to go off once a skill. The idea is the same though. hitch on to something that happens once per skill to make it once per skill

So first off, thank you for the reply and idea! I just experimented with this a bit, unfortunately I get a crash with the error "applyItemUserEffect is not a function".
So I created a BattleManager.applyItemUserEffect function and it'll read that, but then crash with "this.item is not a function"...for which I then created a BattleManager.item function, but it crashes due to "object is undefined".
Correct me if I'm wrong and I very well could be, but it seems to me that your idea could work but it's going to require writing new versions of a hefty amount of functions, so I'd like to find a simpler solution if possible.
After learning the result of the BattleManager changes, I'd ideally like to target a function within rmmz_objects.js so that I can keep changes targeted to where they need to be. Though if that is possible, well, that remains to be seen.
However, I will try and follow your line of thinking.
There must be something earlier I can target than Game_Action.prototype.apply to get the TP gain to fire at the start of the use of a skill or item itself.
Thank you again, it is very much appreciated

posts.body:
Niniann said:
I'm going to try turning this into an alias and see if everything goes smoothly, as it does appear that Visustella may have changed the function and is using it for something, likely in the battle core, and I don't want to burn whatever it is they're already cooking.
Click to expand...
the problem with aliasing that function instead of overwriting is that you dont actually want the prior code to run in this case. when you make and call an alias, youre essentially adding extra code onto a pre-existing function. if you choose to use an alias here, the prior code will still run but it will run alongside your new code. So not only will each hit still generate TP, but the skill will also gain an extra hit's worth of TP on the first hit.
thats why my intention was to overwrite it, but i didnt expect VS to do anything to that function. its your call as to whether or not you want to overwrite it, but keep in mind that if you never utilize whatever part of the plugin uses it, you may not run into an issue over changing it.
that being said
Niniann said:
Here is the error report:
Click to expand...
its being used within the skills and states plugin. And as said before, your error is because a function is not getting a battler thats supposed to be supplied. the original function had a target parameter that i said was not used. Even though the base engine doesnt use it, it would seem like its not the case for the VS plugin. change
Niniann said:
NinGainTPPlugin.call(this);
Click to expand...
to
Code:
NinGainTPPlugin.call(this, target);
so that it is supplied with the target.
when youre writing aliases for functions, you generally want so set it up so that it still passes all the arguments it got called with into the base function.
